paragraphs: Friend, here's what David teaches me in this song. Fear doesn't get the last word when the LORD is your light, your salvation and the stronghold of your life (Psalm 27:1). David isn't pretending the trouble isn't there. An army, a war and false witnesses are all in this song, and he still says, "my heart will not fear" (Psalm 27:3).

So where does that kind of courage come from? I think it comes from what David wants most. He says there's one thing he's asked of the LORD: to dwell in His house, gaze on His beauty and seek Him (Psalm 27:4). Then he calls out, "Hear, O LORD, my voice when I call," and says even if his father and mother forsake him, the LORD will receive him (Psalm 27:7, 10). When what you want most is the LORD Himself, a scary day has a lot less room to boss you around.

And then comes that little word, "Still," and David is certain he'll see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living (Psalm 27:13). That's why his song ends the way it does: "Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous. Wait patiently for the LORD!" (Psalm 27:14). Friend, I know waiting is hard, and I spent plenty of time in the back of a junk drawer learning that. So when your own day of trouble shows up, do what David does: seek His face, and wait with courage, because the LORD is worth the wait.
